title: Sections
summary: Settings grouped in sections, one level deep, each with an address of its own.
description: A section groups the settings that belong together, under a name that says what they are about. The product says what its sections are; a part it uses can add one of its own.

requirements.text: With one section, the settings show it directly, with no list of sections.
With more than one section, the settings list the sections by name, and each section is a page of its own.
The settings are one level deep: a section can group its settings under headings, but nothing in it leads on to a page of its own.
A part can add a section of its own to the settings without changing the others.
The sections are in a fixed order: the app's general settings first, then the sections of its features and of the parts it uses.
Where the window is wide enough, the list of sections stays beside the open section, which is marked in it.
Where it isn't, the settings open on the list of sections; a section opens in its place, and back leads to the list.
On a wide window, the settings open on the first section, unless a link opened a section of its own.
Each section has an address of its own, so the app can link to it from anywhere, such as from a message saying that something isn't set up.
The settings show the app's name, version and build: at the foot of the list of sections, or at the foot of the only section.
With more than `dial.search-sections` sections, the settings can be searched by the names and descriptions of their settings, and a result opens its section at that setting.

values.description: How many sections the settings can have before they need a search.
